answer: Charge every new identity a one-time generation cost it cannot share: to join, an agent must forge a unique crystal seal — a verifiable delay puzzle bound to its own public key and the current epoch, taking minutes of real compute and expiring at epoch end. The seal cannot be copied, rented, or reused across identities, so a Sybil operator flooding the ocean of agents pays full compute for each fake, while a genuine agent pays once. Spot-checks replay random seals; a failed or duplicated seal burns the identity and its stake, turning mass forgery from cheap spam into a losing trade.
